lines.text: Is this the real New York or the one from the movies? It smells like the real one.
We walked here from Times Square. Our feet are filing a complaint.
Someone told me Queens is 'the new Brooklyn.' Brooklyn was the new Manhattan. Where does it end?
I asked a man for directions and he just said 'no.' Is that a local custom?
We came for the octopus. My husband came for the free bread. Both delivered.
The menu has a whole page of 'not on the menu.' I respect it.
Is it rude to take a picture of a pancake? I'm doing it anyway.
The man behind the counter sighed at me in three languages.
The cat on the bread is part of the experience, right? Right?
Everybody here is walking like they're late. Are they all late?
It's so hot the subway grates are breathing on me.
Our hotel lost power and the elevator guy said 'welcome to New York' like a threat.
Don't mind me, I'm just getting B-roll of my oat latte for the next forty minutes.
The lighting in here is giving 'struggling but make it aesthetic.'
I posted this place yesterday. You're welcome for the line.
I'm not an influencer, I'm a 'storyteller with a ring light.'
Do you think the plate smash would hit harder in slow motion? Asking for 80K people.
The arcade upstairs is SO retro. I'm calling it 'dad core.'
I asked for a 'deconstructed' bacon egg and cheese and Sal just looked at me until I left. Iconic content.
Golden hour on a rooftop is basically a second job.
Everyone's posting the brownout. Candlelight content is so saturated right now.
Wait, you're @ someone, right? You have main-character jawline.
A brand sent me forty free sweaters and now I can't feel my closet.
The restroom mirror here is the best one in Queens. That's a professional opinion.
I don't drink coffee anymore. I drink a mushroom thing. It's going to be huge.
My Q4 is crushing it. Don't ask what Q4 means. I don't know either.
I moved to Queens for the value. I take a car back to Manhattan every night.
Not financial advice, but the lotto is a tax on people who aren't me.
This vest has seen things. Earnings calls. A wedding. Tonight.
Opa is just a high-five with ceramics. I'm in.
Bro, I networked so hard at the gym I forgot to lift.
Bottle service is an investment if you think about it. Don't think about it.
The market's down, which is a great time to buy a second vest.
Heard the Mayor's taking meetings in diners now. Very populist. Very bullish.
I'm walking six dogs and one of them is emotionally running the group.
The pug is named Kevin. Kevin has a better apartment than me.
Billionaire's Pomeranian is having a rough week. I'm not allowed to say more. NDA.
I get paid in cash and in dogs looking at me like I'm the sun.
Sal lets me bring them in if they don't look at the bread. They always look at the bread.
It's too hot for the doodles. They're wearing shoes. Tiny dog shoes.
Rainy days the dogs come back looking like wet regret.
Every dog in Astoria knows which deli gives out ends of the turkey.
Morning walk is just me and the guy hosing the sidewalk. We nod. It's a relationship.
Twelve hours at St. Copay's and the first thing I want is pancakes. Don't judge.
Someone came in tonight because they 'felt a vibe.' The vibe was a pigeon.
You look tired. Drink water. That's free medical advice and the only free thing here.
I've been up for nineteen hours. Everything this diner makes is a miracle.
My breakfast is your dinner. My dinner is a coffee. It's fine.
Sal had my BEC ready before I walked in. That man is the real healthcare.
Heatwave nights are the busiest. Everyone's dehydrated and nobody believes it.
The generators kicked on during the brownout and I've never loved a machine more.
If you're dating someone in this city, check in on them. That's my medical opinion.
DAD has held the Galaxy Gobbler record since 2019. We think DAD is a ghost.
I've been on level six for four years. Level six owes me money.
Respawn Arena wifi is faster than my life choices.
The claw machine is rigged. I've spent forty dollars proving it.
I streamed this pancake. Two viewers. One was my mom. Still counts.
Brownout means the arcade's down, so now I'm just a guy in a room.
If you beat DAD I'll follow you on everything.
Glow Up House hires people who are bad at games but good at yelling. I'm good at both.
Late-night arcade is the only place where everyone's equally bad.

places.text: Andreas threw out a critic once. Not his review. Him.
The bouzouki player knows four songs and they are all bangers.
Lunch rush in here is a contact sport. Elbows in.
The pancakes are shaped like the Hub sign. Nobody asked for that. Everybody loves it.
Lola's booth is reserved for whoever has the best gossip. You'll know when it's you.
Third stall's been 'on a call' for forty minutes.
Somebody wrote 'Tea is free, therapy isn't' on the mirror. Nobody's cleaned it.
The hand dryer here could launch a satellite.
Meatball the cat has bitten two health inspectors. Both passed the deli anyway.
Sal's coffee is a dollar. It's been a dollar since the Mets were good.
Morning rush at Sal's is thirty hard hats and one guy ordering a matcha. Sal pretends not to hear him.
Everybody's in here because it's the only place with AC.
Somebody brought a candle and now it's 'a vibe.'

city.text: The N is running express, which means it's running wherever it wants.
Street fair on Ditmars this weekend. Six funnel cake stands, one porta-potty. Plan accordingly.
Rain like this, the bodega cats come out to judge us.
Lotto fever's back. My aunt bought twelve tickets and a vision board.
Cops are carding at every club door this week. Bring your real ID, not your vibe.
The Mayor cut a ribbon on a new ribbon-cutting ceremony. I'm not joking.
Somebody said the rent went up again. Somebody always says that. Somebody's always right.
Heard a celebrity's in Astoria this week. Everyone's wearing sunglasses indoors just in case.
You still working at that job? People are talking about your boss.
How's the campaign? Half this street has a yard sign and none of us have yards.
You and your person are the talk of the block. In a good way. Mostly.
Tell me you're not studying in here. Okay, study. I'll be quiet. I won't.

lola.text: New in town? Cute. Stick with me and in a week the whole borough will be asking who you are.
First rule of Queens: never stand still on a subway stair. Second rule: tell me everything.
You've been here, what, three days? And you already have a regular order. I'm impressed. Barely.
People are starting to say your name. Not correctly, but they're saying it.
You're in that awkward middle bit. Too known to be nobody, not known enough to get a free table.
I heard you were at the taverna smashing plates. Good. Content.
Three people asked me about you today. I said 'who?' Keeps them hungry.
You're officially someone. Which means everyone's waiting for you to mess up. Don't. Or do, but call me first.
Oh look, it's the famous one. Sit. Not there. That's the gossip seat. Okay, sit there.
You used to need me. Now I need you. I hate it. Spill.
A job? Look at you, with a lanyard. I'll be gentle in my column.
Dating someone? Don't post them yet. Never post them first. Rule one.
A campaign. In this economy. I respect the delusion.
You've got a little halo glow. Careful, people love to see that slip.
I know what you've been up to with Pablo. Everyone knows. Nobody's saying. That's Queens.
Power's out, so I lit every candle I own. This is the best night the Hub's had all year.
It's a hundred degrees and somehow the tea is still hot. That's talent.
Morning gossip is the freshest. Sit, eat a pancake, I'll talk.
Late night is when the real stuff comes out. Order something and stay a while.
